note: F02, settled by the read the held rows named. The hero's real paint is #F3F4F6 on both boards, so the INSPECTOR SAMPLE was the wrong half — exactly as the hold predicted. The held rows that would have painted the hero #1A56DB and its text white are superseded and must stay held.

rows.why: F02 · RESOLVED BY MEASUREMENT. resolve-and-read returned 'H 52:159 FRAME 500,111303,680,250 #F3F4F6 FILL/FIXED VERTICAL Hero — SELECTED parent=52:153 site page' — the selected hero's own fill is #F3F4F6, a light grey, which is what every render of this board has shown. The Inspector's Background Fill therefore names a colour the selected element does not have, and the repair is to correct the readout, not the canvas. Confirming the hold's reasoning: #1A56DB is Buildrik's OWN accent (DESIGN.md's single accent), and painting a mock customer site's hero in the product's brand blue would have been a category error — and unrecoverable, because op:fill has no expect guard and the true value would never have been recorded.

F02 · the same correction on the second board. resolve-and-read returned 'H 199:292 FRAME 3620,476,680,250 #F3F4F6 FILL/FIXED VERTICAL Hero — SELECTED parent=199:286 site page'. Identical fill, identical defect, identical fix. Both hero frames are FILL/FIXED inside a 'site page' parent, so neither was individually painted — the grey is the page's, which is further evidence the blue was a sample value typed into the inspector rather than a colour anything on the canvas ever had.
